Complete assignment thoroughly:

# Target
Worktree `/Users/bnjoroge/preloop-gh-app-api-compat`. Files (ONLY these): `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/dispatch.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/broker.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/routes.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/errors.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/runs.rs`. Do NOT touch openapi.rs, dispatch_tests.rs, github_app.rs, or any docs.

# Change (five validated items)
1. **stable_id uses DefaultHasher (correctness)** — `fn stable_id(value: &str) -> u64` in dispatch.rs (~line 670): `DefaultHasher` is explicitly NOT guaranteed stable across Rust releases, and these ids are returned to clients (workflow/run ids) and persisted. Replace with a stable SHA-256 truncation: `use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};` (sha2 is already a workspace dep), hash `value.as_bytes()`, take the first 8 bytes as a little-endian u64 (or `u64::from_le_bytes`). Keep the function signature and the doc comment's intent (deterministic, stable across restarts AND toolchains). Grep the repo for tests asserting specific `stable_id` outputs (dispatch_tests.rs has some; you may NOT edit dispatch_tests.rs — if a test asserts a specific numeric id, report it in your summary with the line numbers so the coordinator can update it; if a test only asserts determinism/equality, leave it).
2. **git refs starting with '-' (security)** — `fetch_workflows_at` in github.rs (~line 571-628): `git_ref` flows into `git rev-parse`, `git ls-tree`, `git show` as a positional arg; a client-supplied ref beginning with `-` is parsed by git as an option. Add an explicit guard BEFORE `rev-parse --verify`: skip ref resolution (fall through to the checked-out-tree path with the existing warn!) when `git_ref.starts_with('-')`. Preserve all valid-ref behavior.
3. **ls-tree/git show failures are silent (correctness)** — same function: after a successful `rev-parse`, if `git ls-tree` exits non-zero, return an error (`anyhow::bail!` or `.with_context(...)`) instead of falling through to the checked-out tree; and inside the per-file loop, if `git show <ref>:<path>` exits non-zero for any listed path, return an error instead of silently omitting that workflow. Preserve the existing fallback ONLY for the rev-parse failure case (ref not present locally).
4. **broker bypasses mint-failure policy (correctness)** — `mint_dispatch_github_token` in broker.rs (~line 990): when `select_app_for_repo` returns None, currently `return Ok(None)` silently. Change: if `request.untrusted`, keep returning `Ok(None)` (existing comment about untrusted jobs applies). Otherwise, if a default App exists (`shared.state.github_app`), apply ITS mint-failure policy via the existing `crate::github_app::fallback_token(app.mint_failure, app.pat_fallback.clone())` — on Ok(token) return `Some(MintedGitHubToken { token, effective_permissions: None })`, on Err map to `ApiError::bad_gateway` like the existing fallback path does. If no default App exists either, keep `Ok(None)`. Log a `warn!` when falling back because no registered App covers the repository. Preserve the existing behavior for the Some(app) path untouched.
5. **typed trigger-mismatch signal (maintainability)** — `is_trigger_mismatch` in dispatch.rs (~line 445) matches error MESSAGE text; the mismatch error is built in runs.rs (~line 261-264, `ApiError::bad_request(format!("workflow does not match event `{}`", ...))`). Fix: add a discriminant to `ApiError` in errors.rs — e.g. a `pub(crate) kind: ApiErrorKind` field with a `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub(crate) enum ApiErrorKind { BadRequest, TriggerMismatch }` (default `BadRequest`), plus a constructor `pub(crate) fn trigger_mismatch(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self` that sets status 400 + kind TriggerMismatch. Update runs.rs to construct the mismatch error with `ApiError::trigger_mismatch(...)` (same message text). Rewrite `is_trigger_mismatch` in dispatch.rs to check `error.kind() == ApiErrorKind::TriggerMismatch` (add a `pub(crate) fn kind(&self) -> ApiErrorKind` accessor). Verify every `ApiError` construction in errors.rs sets `kind: ApiErrorKind::BadRequest` (the struct literal sites) or use `#[derive(Default)]` on the enum and `#[derive(Default)]` field... simplest: give ApiErrorKind a `Default` impl with BadRequest and mark the struct field `#[default]`-consistent. Ensure no other callers construct ApiError via struct literal without the new field.
6. **dispatch routes: single auth layer (security-by-construction)** — routes.rs (~line 320-351): the four `/repos/...` routes each repeat `route_layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(shared.clone(), crate::dispatch_auth::require_dispatch_auth))`. Build a nested sub-router with the four routes (same handlers, same paths) and ONE `route_layer(...)` on the sub-router, then `.merge(sub_router)` into the main router chain (match the surrounding router builder style — it is a chain of `.route(...)`/`.merge(...)` calls on one Router; check how the router is assembled and merge accordingly). Preserve exact paths and handler functions; no behavior change. If the router is built via a single `Router::new().route(...).route(...)` chain, restructure minimally: `let dispatch_api = Router::new().route(...).route(...).route(...).route(...).route_layer(...);` then `.merge(dispatch_api)` in the chain.

# Acceptance
- Compile-read coherent; no undefined symbols; no new deps; no test edits (report test-assert dependencies instead).
- Report per item: what changed, exact functions, and any dispatch_tests.rs assertions that depend on stable_id values (line numbers).

items.title: git refs starting with '-'
